page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with a high ratio of memory to compute. The server provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC core running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 32 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system RAM, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU, accompanied by a bundled 480 GB local NVMe SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete GPU accelerators on this instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded processing capabilities alongside the throughput limitations inherent in a two-thread environment. In single-core evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 3429.67, landing in the top tier, paired with a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2116.0. Single-threaded data throughput showed high responsiveness, recording 31.96 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.41 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate parallel throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU count, as reflected in a multi-core Geekbench score of 3772.0, a PassMark CPU score of 5983.03, and static web serving throughput of 2.19 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost and resource efficiency perspective, the voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd balances dedicated CPU time, fast local NVMe storage, and elevated memory density without the overhead of paying for unneeded vCPUs. The primary architectural tradeoff is total parallel compute scale; multi-threaded compiles, large matrix transformations, and high-concurrency web serving will saturate the single physical core. Consequently, this server is well configured for memory-heavy single-threaded workloads, moderate in-memory caching layers, background data staging, and lightweight database applications requiring dedicated execution cores and low-latency storage.
